claims.text: ML-guided liquid-phase sintering with a small addition of glass-forming additives can lower the required sintering temperature for powder-based materials.
The proposed low-temperature process can still achieve effective densification.
The proposed low-temperature process can maintain desirable microstructural properties.
The powder should be modified with 2–3 wt% glass-forming sintering aids.
A machine-learning model can optimize the additive concentration and sintering parameters.
A dwell time of 10–15 minutes is suitable for the proposed process.
The proposed process can reduce the sintering temperature from approximately 1200°C to approximately 750°C.
Glass-forming additives reduce the local melting point at particle boundaries.
The reduced local melting point causes a localized liquid phase to form at particle boundaries.
The localized liquid phase enhances diffusion.
The localized liquid phase fills voids and promotes particle rearrangement.
Enhanced diffusion, void filling, and particle rearrangement accelerate densification at temperatures below those required for conventional solid-state sintering.
Sintering near 750°C with the additives will produce densification comparable to conventional sintering near 1200°C.
Sintering near 750°C with the additives will maintain or improve microstructural integrity relative to conventional high-temperature sintering.
Conventional sintering of the same powder without additives requires approximately 1200°C to achieve densification.
The effectiveness of the proposed method varies with powder composition, additive distribution, and process scale.
Errors in additive performance or machine-learning predictions could reduce the effectiveness of the process.
Optimization is uncertain because material systems vary and the machine-learning training dataset is limited.
